name: s1_d_readers
title: Three readers get the same activation and never the prompt
caption: Each reader receives only the layer-42 activation h at the read token. The NLA has h added at a marker inside its actor prompt and writes an explanation; its critic rebuilds h from those words, and RL rewards words that survive the rebuild. Oracle Lens has h written into one slot character's embedding and writes bullets; the J-lens generates nothing and lists the top tokens of W_U·J_42·h.

notes: Diagram, no data. NLA actor prompt (from notes/wsbench_internals.md 1.5, abbreviated there with '...'; nla_meta.yaml is not in the repo): 'You are a meticulous AI researcher ... We will pass the vector enclosed in <concept> tags ... The explanation consists of 2-3 text snippets ... <concept>[marker U+321C]</concept> Please provide an explanation.' The NLA's h is norm-matched and added at the marker token after block 1. The marker glyph U+321C is not in the figure font, so it is drawn as [h]. The talk script's NLA carrier text quotes experiments/06_resolving_decomposition/data/nla_instruction.txt, which is the TextNLA / warm-start instruction, not the actor prompt: fix the script. Oracle Lens prompt, verbatim: 'An activation vector from layer 42 of a language model is enclosed in activation tags: <activation>X</activation>. Produce distinct concepts that encode this activation, each as a '- ' bullet on its own line.' (slot = an enclosed ideograph, id 158983 for Qwen3.6, embedding replaced by alpha*unit(h), alpha 16000); Oracle Lens was trained at layers 20 to 60 in steps of 4, so layer 42 is off its grid. J-lens: the J-space is the top 1,536 directions at layer 42 (= 4 r*, r* = 384); W_U · J · h is cosine-normalised. Critic input (nla.py): 'Summary of the following text: <text>{e}</text> <summary>'.
